text:
Reviewed the whole repo (`src`, tests, fixtures, packaging, docs). Tests pass: `12 passed`; only warning is pytest cache creation failing because `/work` is read-only.

Overall score: **5/10**. It is small and readable, but I would not approve it as-is because several reporting results can be materially wrong and failed ingests can still mutate the database.

Key Slurm compatibility issues are real, not stylistic: Slurm documents elapsed as `[DD-[HH:]]MM:SS`, state values including `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, possible `+` suffixes on state display, `-p` output with a trailing pipe, and `-T` truncation for exact interval accounting. The current parser/query layer does not handle those cases correctly. ([slurm.schedmd.com](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacct.html))

Findings:

| Severity | File:lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| high | `src/jobwatch/cli.py:83-98` | Failed ingests still commit valid rows before the malformed-row threshold returns nonzero. |
| high | `src/jobwatch/store.py:114,130,161,198-199` | Time-window reports use full-job `COALESCE(end,start,submit)` filtering, so period usage is over/under-counted instead of overlap/truncated accounting. |
| high | `src/jobwatch/store.py:11,123-135,152-166` | Failure reporting misses real Slurm failure states such as `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `NODE_FAIL`, `CANCELLED`, `PREEMPTED`, and suffixed states. |
| high | `src/jobwatch/parsing.py:91-106` | GPU parsing sums every `gres/gpu*` key, so typed plus aggregate TRES values can double-count GPU-hours. |
| medium | `src/jobwatch/parsing.py:71-88` | `Elapsed` parsing rejects valid Slurm forms such as `MM:SS` and `DD-MM:SS`. |
| medium | `src/jobwatch/parsing.py:145` | State normalization only uppercases; it does not canonicalize short states or strip Slurm’s `+` overflow suffix. |
| medium | `src/jobwatch/parsing.py:109-117` | Timestamp normalization stores raw strings and accepts mixed naive/offset ISO values, making SQLite string comparisons unreliable. |
| medium | `src/jobwatch/parsing.py:182-186` | Strict header equality rejects common `sacct -p` parsable output with a trailing delimiter or extra requested columns. |
| medium | `src/jobwatch/store.py:26-49` | SQLite schema has no migration/version tracking, so future schema changes will be brittle. |
| low | `src/jobwatch/store.py:18-20` | Default database directory is created with process umask instead of an explicit private mode for local accounting data. |
| low | `src/jobwatch/formatting.py:17-29` | Table rendering has no max-width or row-shape validation, so long/unexpected fields can produce unusable output or exceptions. |
| medium | `tests/test_cli.py:16-20,28-32` | CLI tests mostly assert strings are present, not report totals, so major accounting regressions can pass. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **180 lines**. That includes parser fixes, failure-state canonicalization, transactional ingest validation, interval-aware report queries, schema migration scaffolding, and focused tests.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this PR as-is.**

issues.description: Failed ingests still commit valid rows before the malformed-row threshold returns nonzero.
Time-window reports use full-job timestamp filtering, causing inaccurate period usage and failure windows.
Failure reporting misses real Slurm failure states such as OUT_OF_MEMORY, NODE_FAIL, CANCELLED, PREEMPTED, and suffixed states.
GPU TRES parsing can double-count typed plus aggregate gres/gpu entries.
Elapsed parsing rejects valid Slurm forms such as MM:SS and DD-MM:SS.
State normalization does not canonicalize short states or strip Slurm display suffixes.
Raw mixed timestamp strings make SQLite chronological comparisons unreliable.
Strict header equality rejects common sacct parsable output variants.
SQLite schema has no migration or version tracking for future changes.
Default database directory permissions rely on process umask instead of explicit private mode.
Table rendering has no max-width or row-shape validation.
CLI tests assert presence of labels but not accounting totals or edge-case correctness.
